title: Feudalism
examples: What was the main difference between a lord and a vassal?
How did serfs fit into the feudal system?
Can you explain the obligations in feudalism?

explain.say: Today we are learning about feudalism in the Middle Ages. Say this word with me: feudalism.
First we look at the social hierarchy. This was a very structured way of life. The king was at the very top of this structure.
Next we learn about the relationship between lords and vassals. A vassal swore loyalty to a lord for protection. This was a key part of the system.
The next idea is obligations. Peasants owed labor and goods to the lord. This was their main duty in exchange for protection.
For a concrete example, a knight was a type of vassal. He swore fealty to a lord in exchange for a small estate. This gave him status and land.
In real life, think about your school. You have obligations to your classmates. You must follow the school rules to learn well.

faq.q: What was the main difference between a serf and a peasant?
faq.a: A serf was legally bound to the land and could not leave it. A peasant might have more freedom to move, though they were still agricultural workers.

faq.q: Did everyone in the feudal system own land?
faq.a: No, only the highest lords and the king owned the largest amounts of land. Lower classes worked the land owned by others.

faq.q: What did the king actually do in this system?
faq.a: The king was theoretically at the top, owning all the land. He granted portions of it out to powerful lords who swore allegiance to him.

faq.q: Why did the system rely so much on loyalty?
faq.a: Because there was no strong central government, personal oaths of loyalty were the main way people protected themselves and maintained order.

faq.q: Did the obligations change over time?
faq.a: Yes, the system slowly changed over centuries. Economic growth and new ideas eventually weakened the strict bonds of feudalism.
asks: What caused the system to break down?

facts: Feudalism was a social and political system common in medieval Europe.
The hierarchy ranged from the King down to the serfs.
Vassals received land from lords in exchange for military service.
Serfs were typically tied to the land they worked on.

quiz.say: A vassal swore loyalty to a lord to receive what?
quiz.why: The core exchange in vassalage was land in return for loyalty and service.

wrong.0: While education was sometimes granted, the fundamental requirement was military or labor service.
wrong.2: Money was not the primary currency of obligation in this system.
wrong.3: While freedom was desired, the initial exchange was land for service, not just freedom.

quiz.say: What did serfs owe the lord?
quiz.why: Serfs owed physical work and a portion of their harvest to the lord.

wrong.0: Military service was usually the obligation of the knightly class, not the serfs.
wrong.1: Oaths were important, but they were backed up by tangible work and goods.
wrong.3: While taxes were paid, the primary obligation was often physical labor on the lord's land.

quiz.say: Which group sat at the very top of the feudal hierarchy?
quiz.why: The King was considered the ultimate source of authority and land ownership.

wrong.0: Knights were important warriors, but they were vassals to someone higher up.
wrong.1: Peasants were at the bottom, providing the labor that supported the whole system.
wrong.3: Lords were powerful, but they received their authority from the King.
